cvVsResume.title: CV vs Resume: Key Differences and When to Use Each
cvVsResume.description: Understand the difference between a CV and a resume — length, purpose, content and formatting — and which document RMUTL students should send for internships, jobs and graduate applications.

cvVsResume.title: CV vs Resume: What's the Difference?
cvVsResume.subtitle: Understanding when to use each document can make or break your application.
cvVsResume.resumeDesc: A resume is a concise, targeted document typically 1-2 pages long. It highlights your relevant skills, work experience, and achievements tailored to a specific job position. Resumes are the standard for most industry and corporate job applications. They focus on brevity and relevance, omitting details that don't directly support your candidacy for the role.
cvVsResume.cvDesc: A CV (Curriculum Vitae) is a comprehensive document that provides an in-depth overview of your entire academic and professional history. Unlike a resume, a CV can span multiple pages and includes detailed sections on education, publications, research, presentations, awards, and professional affiliations. CVs are primarily used in academic, research, and international job applications.

table.contentResume: Relevant skills and experience for a specific role
table.contentCv: Full academic history, publications, research, awards

cvVsResume.whenDesc: Use a resume when applying for jobs in the private sector, corporate roles, startups, or most government positions. Use a CV when applying for academic positions, research roles, graduate school, fellowships, or positions in countries outside the US where CVs are the standard (e.g., Europe, UK, parts of Asia).
cvVsResume.tipDesc: Always check the application requirements carefully. Some employers explicitly state which document they prefer. Having both versions prepared ensures you're ready for any opportunity.
cvVsResume.reference: Reference: JobsDB Thailand — CV vs Resume Guide

howToUse.title: How to Use RMUTL Resume
howToUse.subtitle: Follow these simple steps to create your professional resume.

step1.title: 1. Sign Up / Sign In
step1.desc: Create a free account or sign in to access your dashboard. Your resumes are saved securely in the cloud so you can access them from anywhere.

step2.title: 2. Create a New Resume
step2.desc: Click "New Resume" from your dashboard. Choose between a Resume (1-2 pages, industry-focused) or a CV (comprehensive academic document).

step3.title: 3. Edit Your Content
step3.desc: Use the real-time editor to fill in your information. Sections include contact details, summary, experience, education, skills, and more. Changes appear instantly as you type.

step4.title: 4. Leverage AI Features
step4.desc: Use our AI-powered tools: Auto-Fill to populate sections from an existing resume, and ATS Score to check how well your resume will perform with Applicant Tracking Systems.

step5.title: 5. Share & Export
step5.desc: Once you're happy with your resume, share it with a public link or export it as a PDF. Recruiters can view your resume online without downloading any files.

step6.title: 6. Manage Your Resumes
step6.desc: Access all your resumes from the Dashboard. You can rename, duplicate, or delete documents. Keep multiple versions tailored for different industries or roles.
